answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy rests on bonded stake: each identity escrows collateral before it can serve or vouch. Every attestation becomes a claim backed by that deposit, so when auditors detect fake accounts the stake is slashed and paid out. An attacker therefore pays rent per identity and earns less as the network grows. Forging a quill of invented peers, or hiding a karst of duplicate accounts to skew reputation, only enlarges exposure. Like a wharf charging each vessel a deposit to dock, the system prices deception rather than trusting signatures.
